title: Weather Radar Picture Quality and Missing Windshear Alerting on Approach in Convective Conditions

ata.title: Independent Position Determining — Weather Radar Transceiver

abstract: Operator request about a weather radar picture that crews describe as coarse and slow to build below three thousand feet, and about the absence of the predictive windshear alerting the operator's other fleets provide on approach.

sections.request: Our crews fly into a lot of convective weather in the wet season and they have started asking why the picture on this fleet is so much coarser than on the rest of our aircraft. The specific complaints are that cells close in take too long to paint, that the ground return below three thousand feet swamps the cell we are actually interested in, and that there is no alerting at all for windshear on the approach, which the crews are used to having and now have to do without. We have also had four reports of the picture freezing for ten or fifteen seconds and then catching up. Two of our captains have filed reports saying they went around on the basis of what they could see out of the window rather than what the radar showed, and that is not a good position for us to be in.
sections.background: We took this fleet on three years ago and the crews came off a type where the predictive alerting was standard, so some of this is expectation. But the ground return complaint is not expectation, it is measurable, and our own flight data shows the tilt being worked far harder on this fleet than on the others in the same weather. We have had one transceiver replaced for the freezing complaint and the shop found nothing. Our training department has asked for a fleet decision because they are currently teaching two different approaches to the same weather.
sections.expected_outcome: Predictive windshear alerting on approach, and a picture in the last two thousand feet that our crews trust without working the tilt. We would like it retrofittable across the whole fleet in one campaign rather than aircraft by aircraft, because the training case only works when every aeroplane behaves the same way.

type_data.business_justification: Two filed crew reports of go-arounds flown without usable radar guidance, a training department teaching two different techniques across one operator's fleets, and a measurable increase in manual tilt activity compared with the operator's other types in the same weather.
